title: Rekke å eller ha tid til å — deadlines and available time
goal: Choose whether successful completion before a cutoff matters or only available time matters.

objectives.statement: Choose whether successful completion before a cutoff matters or only available time matters.

spans.value: Nora and Emil work in the same office. They are due at a customer meeting across town, but Nora also needs to send a revised budget before they leave.
Møtet begynner klokka halv tre. Rekker vi å ta bussen som går om tjue minutter?

blocks.translation: The meeting starts at half past two. Will we manage to catch the bus that leaves in twenty minutes?

spans.value: Ja, hvis vi går om ti minutter. Men rekker du å sende budsjettet først?

blocks.translation: Yes, if we leave in ten minutes. But will you manage to send the budget first?

spans.value: Det tror jeg. Jeg må bare kontrollere to tall. Har du tid til å se på den siste siden?

blocks.translation: I think so. I only need to check two figures. Do you have time to look at the last page?

spans.value: Ja, det har jeg. Jeg har ingen andre oppgaver akkurat nå.

blocks.translation: Yes, I do. I don’t have any other tasks right now.

spans.value: Flott. Hvis vi samarbeider, rekker vi å bli ferdige før bussen går.

blocks.translation: Great. If we work together, we’ll manage to finish before the bus leaves.

spans.value: Send meg dokumentet. Jeg har tid til å lese siden nå, men ikke til å skrive om hele teksten.

blocks.translation: Send me the document. I have time to read the page now, but not to rewrite the entire text.

spans.value: Two different questions about time appear here. Nora asks whether they can complete actions before particular cutoffs: sending the budget before leaving and finishing before the bus departs. For those questions, she uses
rekke å
. She also asks whether Emil has some time available to help. For that, she uses
ha tid til å
Use
rekke å + infinitive
when successful completion before a cutoff matters.

no.value: Rekker du å sende budsjettet før vi går?

en.value: Will you manage to send the budget before we leave?

spans.value: There is a limited period, and the result must be achieved within it. The cutoff may be stated directly, as in før vi går, or it may be clear from the situation.
Use
ha tid til å + infinitive
when you are asking or stating whether time is available for an activity.

no.value: Har du tid til å se på den siste siden?

en.value: Do you have time to look at the last page?

spans.value: Here the main issue is Emil’s availability. Nora wants to know whether his schedule or workload leaves room for the activity.
Both expressions can correspond to English questions with have time, so a word-for-word translation is not enough. Ask what the speaker means:

items.value: Is the key question whether the action can be completed in time? Use
Is the key question whether there is time available for the activity? Use

sections.title: Completion before a cutoff: rekke å

spans.value: The basic frame is:
rekke å + infinitive
The verb after å names the action that must happen within the available period.

no.value: Jeg rekker å sende e-posten før lunsj.

en.value: I’ll manage to send the email before lunch.

no.value: Vi rekker å kjøpe billetter før filmen begynner.

en.value: We’ll manage to buy tickets before the film starts.

no.value: Hun rakk å låse døra før hun løp til bussen.

en.value: She managed to lock the door before she ran to the bus.

spans.value: A cutoff often appears with expressions such as før møtet, innen fredag, før butikken stenger, or før toget går.

no.value: Rekker dere å bli ferdige innen fredag?

en.value: Will you manage to finish by Friday?

no.value: Jeg rekker ikke å handle før butikken stenger.

en.value: I won’t manage to shop before the store closes.

no.value: Rakk han å ringe legen før kontoret stengte?

en.value: Did he manage to call the doctor before the office closed?

spans.value: Sometimes the cutoff remains unstated because everyone already knows it.
At a station, someone might ask:

no.value: Rekker vi å kjøpe kaffe?

en.value: Will we have enough time to buy coffee?

spans.value: The likely cutoff is the train’s departure. The question is not simply whether coffee buying fits somewhere in the day. It is whether the speakers can buy it and still catch the train.
At work, a colleague might say:

no.value: Jeg rekker ikke å lese alt.

en.value: I won’t manage to read everything in time.

spans.value: The deadline could be a meeting that is about to begin or a document that must be returned soon. Even without an explicit før phrase, rekke presents the activity as a race against limited time.
Checkpoint: identify the hidden cutoff

Read several short situations involving a departing bus, a closing shop, a meeting that is about to start, and a report due at the end of the day. For each situation, explain in a few words what event limits the available time.
This activity belongs here because
rekke å
often depends on a cutoff that is understood rather than stated. A successful response would identify the relevant endpoint and show why completing the action before that endpoint matters.

sections.title: Available time: ha tid til å

spans.value: The basic frame is:
ha tid til å + infinitive
Use it when time is treated as part of someone’s availability or capacity.

no.value: Jeg har tid til å hjelpe deg etter lunsj.

en.value: I have time to help you after lunch.

no.value: Har du tid til å snakke litt?

en.value: Do you have time to talk for a bit?

no.value: Vi har ikke tid til å besøke museet i dag.

en.value: We don’t have time to visit the museum today.

no.value: Hun hadde tid til å lage middag hjemme.

en.value: She had time to make dinner at home.

spans.value: The activity may take ten minutes or several hours. The important point is whether the person’s schedule leaves room for it.

no.value: På søndag har jeg tid til å vaske leiligheten.

en.value: On Sunday I have time to clean the apartment.

spans.value: This says that Sunday offers enough available time for cleaning. It does not necessarily present cleaning as a task that must be completed before a particular deadline.
Questions with
har du tid til å
are also common requests.

no.value: Har du tid til å lese gjennom søknaden min?

en.value: Do you have time to read through my application?

spans.value: The speaker is asking about the other person’s availability. The application may eventually have a deadline, but that is not what the expression itself highlights.
Checkpoint: focus on availability
Use short descriptions of people’s schedules to write questions with
har tid til å
. The contexts should include Nora asking Emil for help, a friend checking whether someone can meet after work, and a family member asking for help with dinner.
This practice belongs here because it keeps attention on free time and workload rather than on racing toward an endpoint. A successful response would use
ha tid til å
when the context asks whether an activity fits into someone’s schedule.
The difference becomes clearer when the action stays the same but the time perspective changes.
Reading a document

no.value: Har du tid til å lese rapporten i dag?

en.value: Do you have time to read the report today?

spans.value: The question concerns available time in the person’s day.

no.value: Rekker du å lese rapporten før møtet?

en.value: Will you manage to read the report before the meeting?

spans.value: The question concerns completion before the meeting begins.
Calling someone

no.value: Jeg har tid til å ringe kunden etter lunsj.

en.value: I have time to call the customer after lunch.

spans.value: The speaker has an available period after lunch.

no.value: Jeg rekker å ringe kunden før lunsj.

en.value: I’ll manage to call the customer before lunch.

spans.value: The call can be completed before the stated cutoff.
Shopping

no.value: Vi har tid til å handle i ettermiddag.

en.value: We have time to go shopping this afternoon.

spans.value: Shopping fits into the afternoon schedule.

no.value: Vi rekker å handle før butikken stenger.

en.value: We’ll manage to shop before the store closes.

spans.value: The store’s closing time creates a cutoff.
Finishing work

no.value: Nora har tid til å arbeide med budsjettet nå.

en.value: Nora has time to work on the budget now.

spans.value: She has room in her schedule to do some work on it.

no.value: Nora rekker å gjøre ferdig budsjettet før hun går.

en.value: Nora will manage to finish the budget before she leaves.

spans.value: Finishing the budget must happen before her departure.
Notice how
rekke å
naturally combines with actions that lead to a result: send, finish, catch, submit, buy, or arrive.
Ha tid til å
can also be used with these verbs, but it presents the activity as something that does or does not fit into the speaker’s available time.

no.value: Jeg har tid til å skrive ferdig rapporten i kveld.

en.value: I have time to finish writing the report this evening.

spans.value: This means that the evening provides sufficient available time.

no.value: Jeg rekker å skrive ferdig rapporten før fristen.

en.value: I’ll manage to finish writing the report before the deadline.

spans.value: This emphasizes achieving the result before the deadline.
Checkpoint: choose the intended perspective

Work with paired situations that contain the same action but different intentions. In one version, a person’s schedule is the main issue. In the other, an approaching departure, closing time, meeting, or deadline is the main issue. Supply a complete sentence with the expression that matches each intention.
This controlled contrast belongs here because vocabulary alone cannot determine the choice. A successful response would preserve the action while changing between
ha tid til å
and
rekke å
according to whether availability or timely completion is central.
Negative forms are especially useful because they show what the speaker says is impossible.

no.value: Jeg har ikke tid til å spise frokost.

en.value: I don’t have time to eat breakfast.

spans.value: Breakfast does not fit into the speaker’s available time.

no.value: Jeg rekker ikke å spise frokost før bussen går.

en.value: I won’t manage to eat breakfast before the bus leaves.

spans.value: The speaker may have a few free minutes, but not enough to complete breakfast before the bus departs.
Compare another pair:

no.value: Emil har ikke tid til å kontrollere hele dokumentet.

en.value: Emil doesn’t have time to check the entire document.

spans.value: His available time or workload does not allow it.

no.value: Emil rekker ikke å kontrollere hele dokumentet før Nora må sende det.

en.value: Emil won’t manage to check the entire document before Nora has to send it.

spans.value: The sending time is the cutoff. He may begin checking, but he cannot complete the whole task in time.
This distinction matters because beginning an activity is not the same as completing it before an endpoint.

no.value: Jeg har ti minutter, så jeg har tid til å begynne. Men jeg rekker ikke å bli ferdig.

en.value: I have ten minutes, so I have time to start. But I won’t manage to finish.

spans.value: The first clause describes available time. The second describes failure to reach a result before time runs out.
Checkpoint: explain what fails

For each negative sentence, state whether the problem is lack of room in the schedule or failure to complete the action before a cutoff. Use contexts from Nora and Emil’s afternoon, including checking figures, rewriting text, leaving the office, and catching the bus.

This checkpoint belongs here because negative sentences can sound similar in English. A successful response would identify precisely what the speaker lacks: general available time or enough time to reach the required result.
Using ha tid til å when the deadline is the point
Less suitable for the intended meaning:

no.value: Har vi tid til å bli ferdige før bussen går?

en.value: Do we have time to finish before the bus leaves?

spans.value: This sentence is understandable, but if the intended question is whether the speakers will successfully finish before the bus leaves,
rekker vi å
expresses that perspective more directly.
Preferred for the chapter’s target meaning:

no.value: Rekker vi å bli ferdige før bussen går?

en.value: Will we manage to finish before the bus leaves?

spans.value: Using rekke å for ordinary availability
Less suitable when asking about someone’s schedule:

no.value: Rekker du å hjelpe meg en gang i ettermiddag?

en.value: Will you manage to help me sometime this afternoon?

spans.value: This can suggest an implicit limit or a crowded afternoon. If the speaker simply wants to know whether the other person is available, use:

no.value: Har du tid til å hjelpe meg i ettermiddag?

en.value: Do you have time to help me this afternoon?

spans.value: Copying English have time mechanically
English often uses have time for both ideas.
Do you have time to send it before the meeting?
Norwegian choice depends on the intended focus.

no.value: Rekker du å sende den før møtet?

en.value: Will you manage to send it before the meeting?

spans.value: The meeting is an endpoint, and successful sending before that endpoint is the central issue.
By contrast:

no.value: Har du tid til å arbeide med den i dag?

en.value: Do you have time to work on it today?

spans.value: Here the speaker asks whether the activity fits into the day.
Leaving out parts of the frame
Both target expressions introduce another verb with
å

no.value: Jeg rekker å sende den.

en.value: I’ll manage to send it in time.

no.value: Jeg har tid til å sende den.

en.value: I have time to send it.

spans.value: Keep
til
in
ha tid til å
. The complete frame is not
ha tid å
Emil has checked the final page. Nora is preparing to send the document.
Jeg har tid til å kontrollere ett tall til.

blocks.translation: I have time to check one more figure.

spans.value: Gjør det. Rekker vi å sende dokumentet før vi må gå?

blocks.translation: Do it. Will we manage to send the document before we have to leave?

spans.value: Ja. Men vi har ikke tid til å diskutere formuleringene nå.

blocks.translation: Yes. But we don’t have time to discuss the wording now.

spans.value: Det går bra. Kunden trenger tallene først.

blocks.translation: That’s fine. The customer needs the figures first.

spans.value: A minute later, Nora sends the budget.
Nå er det sendt. Rekker vi å gå til holdeplassen?

blocks.translation: It’s sent now. Will we manage to walk to the bus stop?

spans.value: Ja, hvis vi går med en gang. Vi har tid til å snakke om resten på bussen.

blocks.translation: Yes, if we leave immediately. We have time to talk about the rest on the bus.

spans.value: The two expressions divide the situation neatly. Sending the document and reaching the stop must happen before cutoffs, so Nora uses
rekke å
. Discussing the wording and talking on the bus depend on whether time is available, so Emil uses
ha tid til å
From schedule to deadline
Take a sentence stating that someone has time available for an activity. Add a clear cutoff and rewrite the message so that successful completion before that cutoff becomes central.
Use situations such as reading a message during the afternoon, buying food before a guest arrives, and completing an online form before the system closes.
This activity belongs here because it requires more than replacing one phrase with another. The whole time perspective must change. A successful response would use
rekke å
, retain a natural infinitive after
å
, and make the cutoff relevant to completing the action.

Without looking back, write the two Norwegian frames. Then write one sentence about completing an action before a cutoff and one sentence about having time available for an activity. Make each expression fit its context clearly in Norwegian.

prompt.value: For each situation, write a few words in Norwegian that identify the event limiting the available time and explain why the action must be completed before it. Situations: 1. At a station, you want to buy coffee, but the bus leaves in five minutes. 2. You need to buy food, but the shop closes soon. 3. You need to send an email, and the meeting starts shortly. 4. You need to finish a report, and it is due at the end of the day.

payload.judge_prompt: Check all four situations separately and report evidence for each criterion. Accept concise natural Norwegian wording and equivalent endpoint descriptions.

criteria.instruction: Identifies the relevant endpoint in each of the bus, shop, meeting, and report situations.
Explains for each situation why the action must be completed before that endpoint.

prompt.value: Build the three complete Norwegian questions in order. All three ask about available time, so use ha tid til å. Contexts: 1. Nora asks Emil whether he can help with the figures. 2. A friend asks whether someone can meet after work. 3. A family member asks whether someone can help with dinner.

Build four complete Norwegian sentences in order, with the same action preserved within each pair. Pair 1 concerns reading a message: available time in the afternoon, then completion before a meeting. Pair 2 concerns making lunch: available time after a meeting, then completion before guests arrive. Use ha tid til å for availability and rekke å for timely completion.

explanation.value: Ha tid til å describes available time; rekke å focuses on succeeding before a deadline.

prompt.value: Read the four negative Norwegian sentences. Choose the interpretation set that classifies every sentence correctly. Available-time means lack of room in the schedule; cutoff means inability to complete before an endpoint. 1. Nora har ikke tid til å kontrollere tallene. 2. Nora rekker ikke å skrive om teksten før møtet begynner. 3. Emil har ikke tid til å forlate kontoret. 4. Emil rekker ikke å ta bussen.

options.text: 1: Manglende ferdigstillelse før et tidspunkt (failure to finish before a cutoff); 2: Mangel på tilgjengelig tid (lack of available time); 3: Mangel på tilgjengelig tid (lack of available time); 4: Manglende ferdigstillelse før et tidspunkt (failure to finish before a cutoff).
options.why: This reverses the meanings of the first two sentences.

options.text: 1: Mangel på tilgjengelig tid (lack of available time); 2: Manglende ferdigstillelse før et tidspunkt (failure to finish before a cutoff); 3: Manglende ferdigstillelse før et tidspunkt (failure to finish before a cutoff); 4: Mangel på tilgjengelig tid (lack of available time).
options.why: This reverses the meanings of the third and fourth sentences.

options.text: 1: Manglende ferdigstillelse før et tidspunkt (failure to finish before a cutoff); 2: Manglende ferdigstillelse før et tidspunkt (failure to finish before a cutoff); 3: Manglende ferdigstillelse før et tidspunkt (failure to finish before a cutoff); 4: Manglende ferdigstillelse før et tidspunkt (failure to finish before a cutoff).
options.why: Sentences 1 and 3 describe lack of general available time, not failure against a stated or understood cutoff.

options.text: 1: Mangel på tilgjengelig tid (lack of available time); 2: Manglende ferdigstillelse før et tidspunkt (failure to finish before a cutoff); 3: Mangel på tilgjengelig tid (lack of available time); 4: Manglende ferdigstillelse før et tidspunkt (failure to finish before a cutoff).
options.why: Sentences 1 and 3 use har ikke tid til å for lack of schedule room; sentences 2 and 4 use rekke ikke å for failure against a cutoff, including an understood bus departure.

stem.value: Choose the interpretation set that classifies all four sentences correctly.

prompt.value: Build three complete Norwegian sentences in order. Rewrite each availability-focused situation so timely completion is central. Use rekke å and keep an explicit cutoff: 1. Read a message during the afternoon; a meeting starts. 2. Buy food before a guest arrives. 3. Complete an online form before the system closes.

Build four complete Norwegian sentences in order. Recast each deadline-focused situation as an availability-focused statement or question. Use ha tid til å and make available time, not a deadline, central: 1. Calling a colleague after lunch. 2. Preparing lunch today. 3. Reviewing a document this evening. 4. Visiting a friend this weekend.

Continue the office story in four short Norwegian lines. Write one positive and one negative line about actions Nora and Emil can complete before the bus leaves. Write one positive and one negative line about activities they have time to do during the journey. Use rekke å for the bus-cutoff lines and ha tid til å for the journey-availability lines.

payload.judge_prompt: Check all four lines separately. Accept natural Norwegian variants, but require the requested polarity, time perspective, and target expression in each line.

criteria.instruction: Includes a positive rekke å line connecting completed action with the bus departure.
Includes a negative rekke å line connecting failure to complete an action with the bus departure.
Includes a positive ha tid til å line about an activity during the journey.
Includes a negative ha tid til å line about an activity during the journey.

prompt.value: Write the two Norwegian target frames from this lesson. Then write one Norwegian sentence with the frame for completing an action before a cutoff and one with the frame for having time available for an activity. Make the chosen expression fit its context clearly in Norwegian.

payload.judge_prompt: Check that the response contains both exact taught frames and two natural Norwegian sentences with the required time perspectives. Accept natural Bokmål variants for sentence content, but do not accept swapped perspectives.

criteria.instruction: Writes both Norwegian frames rekke å + infinitive and ha tid til å + infinitive.
Provides one Norwegian sentence centered on completing an action before a cutoff.
Provides one Norwegian sentence centered on available time for an activity.
